proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added the standard Vendor indemnities for breach of law, IBM-caused data incidents and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and removed the "entire obligation" limitation. We can accept the usual IP exclusions and remedies, but not a sole-remedy credit as the only protection.

ops.newText: In addition, IBM will defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Enterprise against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of IBM's breach of applicable law, any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Content or other Customer data caused by IBM, or IBM's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
ops.oldText: This is IBM's entire obligation to Customer with regard to any claim of infringement.

proposal.summary: IBM's indemnity covers third-party IP claims only, and the "entire obligation" language forecloses indemnity for IBM's breach of law, data breaches it causes, and its gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Our position is a Vendor indemnity covering those heads of claim in addition to IP infringement.

quote: IBM will give Customer a credit equal to the amount Customer paid IBM for the applicable Materials or for use of the applicable Base Components up to a maximum of twelve (12) months of applicable charges. This is IBM's entire obligation to Customer with regard to any claim of infringement.
rationale: IBM's indemnity covers third-party IP claims only, and the "entire obligation" language forecloses indemnity for IBM's breach of law, data breaches it causes, and its gross negligence or wilful misconduct. proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own what we pay for: the default should be Type I. We also need the Type II licence widened to a worldwide, perpetual right to use, modify and sublicense for our business (the current "Enterprise", US-only scope is too narrow), and the Type I licence back to IBM limited to internal use.

ops.newText: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type I Materials. Customer retains all right, title and interest in Content and all other Customer data.
ops.oldText: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.

proposal.summary: The default vests ownership of Materials in IBM, and the Type II licence back is limited to use "within Customer's Enterprise only" with "Enterprise" defined as US-located entities and no right to modify or sublicense. Deliverables we pay for should be Customer-owned by default, with at least a perpetual, worldwide licence to use, modify and sublicense. Note also that the Type I licence back to IBM (p0084) permits external distribution and derivative works of our work product.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have raised the floor to USD 1,000,000 and placed indemnities, confidentiality and data/security breaches, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud outside the cap. We also need the exclusion for loss of or damage to our records and data (Section 9.1(c)(2)) deleted — this is a hosting agreement and data loss is the core risk.

ops.newText: up to the greater of $1,000,000 or the charges paid or payable by Customer to IBM for the Services in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the accrual of the first claim related to the Services; provided that this limitation will not apply to a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, or its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud.
ops.oldText: up to the greater of $100,000 or the charges paid by Customer to IBM for the Services in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the accrual of the first claim related to the Services.

proposal.summary: The cap is mutual and 12-months-fees based, which is acceptable in structure, but the floor is only USD 100,000 and there are no carve-outs for confidentiality, data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud. More seriously, IBM excludes all liability for "loss of, or damage to, Customer's ... records or data" (p0114) in a hosting agreement, which is unacceptable. Our position is a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000 with those obligations sitting outside the cap.

ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need to be able to move the agreement to an affiliate as well as a successor, and assignment should be symmetrical — IBM's assignment should require our consent.

ops.newText: Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement, without IBM's consent, to an Affiliate or to a successor organization by merger, consolidation, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets. IBM will not assign this Agreement without Customer's prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld.
ops.oldText: Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor organization by merger, consolidation or acquisition.

proposal.summary: The successor carve-out is helpful but there is no affiliate carve-out for Customer and no restriction at all on IBM's ability to assign. Our position is assignment to affiliates and successors without consent for Customer, with Vendor assignment subject to our consent.

quote: Customer will not assign this Agreement or any of its rights hereunder without the prior written consent of IBM, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor organization by merger, consolidation or acquisition.
rationale: The successor carve-out is helpful but there is no affiliate carve-out for Customer and no restriction at all on IBM's ability to assign. Our position is assignment to affiliates and successors without consent for Customer, with Vendor assignment subject to our consent.

quote: Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others.
rationale: No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binds Customer; the freedom-of-action clause expressly preserves our right to contract with others.

quote: paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
rationale: Customer-payable early termination charges are defined only by cross-reference to the attachments, so their size is unknown. Our position is no liquidated amounts payable by Customer, with a three-months'-fees cap as the fallback; see the redline proposed under termination for convenience.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted "revocable" and extended the licence to Affiliates and contractors acting for us; the licence should end only when the Agreement does.

ops.newText: IBM grants Customer and its Affiliates and contractors acting on Customer's behalf a nonexclusive license to use the Base Components in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement, which license IBM may not revoke except upon termination or expiration of this Agreement in accordance with its terms.
ops.oldText: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement.

proposal.summary: A licence revocable at IBM's discretion, with no coverage for our Affiliates or contractors, is below our floor. The licence should be irrevocable for the term (terminable only with the Agreement) and extend to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf.

quote: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement.
rationale: A licence revocable at IBM's discretion, with no coverage for our Affiliates or contractors, is below our floor. The licence should be irrevocable for the term (terminable only with the Agreement) and extend to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf.

quote: Customer shall not resell the Services, in whole or in part.
rationale: There is no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on our business. The no-resale clause restricts only onward sale of IBM's own Services and is acceptable.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We are content with the one-month convenience right, but the early termination charge must be capped (three months' fees) and prepaid charges refunded, since the amount is set elsewhere and is currently unbounded.

ops.newText: paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, which will not exceed three (3) months' recurring charges for the terminated Services; and IBM will refund any charges prepaid for the period after the effective date of termination.
ops.oldText: paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.

proposal.summary: The one-month convenience right for Customer is acceptable and IBM has no convenience right, which is what we want. However the early termination charges are open-ended by cross-reference and there is no refund of prepaid charges. Our fallback caps any such fee at three months' fees.

quote: paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.

quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b).
rationale: There is no usage or records audit right against Customer. IBM's right to investigate Acceptable Use Policy violations does not give it access to our systems or records, so no redline is needed.

quote: This Agreement will be governed by the substantive laws of the State of New York, without regard for its conflict of laws provisions.
rationale: New York law is our preferred position and there is no arbitration provision. We would ideally add exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, but this is not a blocker.

quote: Charges for applicable Services will be specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms.

quote: Charges can be specified as one-time, installment, recurring, or usage.

ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

quote: Each party is responsible for the supervision, direction, and control of its respective personnel.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have set renewals to 12 months and shortened the notice window to 30 days; we can live with 60 days. Automatic renewal for a further multi-year term on 90 days' notice is outside our range.

ops.newText: will renew automatically for an additional term of twelve (12) months unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least thirty (30) days prior to the end of the then-current term
ops.oldText: will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term

proposal.summary: A 90-day non-renewal window combined with renewals equal in length to the prior term means we could be locked into a further multi-year term by inadvertence. Our position is 12-month renewals with a 30-day opt-out (60 days as fallback) and a capped price uplift.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot exit a hosting arrangement without our data and migration help; we have added six months' transition assistance (90 days is our fallback) and a 30-day data return with certified deletion.

ops.newText: The termination of selected Service Option Attachments will not affect Customer's obligation to pay charges under other Service Option Attachments. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement or any Service Option Attachment for any reason, IBM will (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at IBM's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Content and other Customer data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.
ops.oldText: The termination of selected Service Option Attachments will not affect Customer's obligation to pay charges under other Service Option Attachments.

proposal.summary: The effect-of-termination clause addresses only our payment obligations. For a hosting agreement we need transition assistance and return of our Content/data in a machine-readable format, followed by certified deletion.

quote: Upon the date of termination, all Customer payment obligations accrued hereunder through the date of termination will become due and payable.
rationale: The effect-of-termination clause addresses only our payment obligations. For a hosting agreement we need transition assistance and return of our Content/data in a machine-readable format, followed by certified deletion.
